Duration::mul¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Duration Duration::mul(std::int64_t k) const;
Duration Duration::operator*(std::int64_t k) const;

What It Does¶

Scales a Duration by a plain integer count k — not by another Duration, since “a duration times a duration” isn’t a meaningful elapsed-time value (compare: Series * Series is fine because both sides are unitless numbers; Duration * Duration would need to be an elapsed-time-squared, which nothing here represents). k scales the underlying nanosecond count directly, so it is unit-agnostic — d * 3 triples d regardless of what unit d was originally built from.

Parameters¶

k (std::int64_t)

A plain integer multiplier, applied to the whole Duration (every element, if self is N-D).

Returns¶

Duration A new duration holding the elementwise scaled result.

Examples¶

Example 1. Triple a one-hour duration.

auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
std::cout << pluss::duration::print(one_hour * 3);

Output¶

Duration(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1)
0 days 03:00:00.000000000

1 h * 3 = 3 h.

Notes¶

  • mul(k) and operator*(k) are the same operation — operator* is documented sugar for mul.

  • There is no Duration * Duration overload — see What It Does for why.

See Also¶

  • div: the inverse scaling operation.

  • floordiv: integer (flooring) division by a plain count.

  • mod: remainder after division by a raw nanosecond divisor.
